A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 16-page SYNTHAGENT paper, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered pages match except for the first-page author name and arXiv version/date metadata.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original model evaluations, ablations, and sensitivity experiments in Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–6, including additional empirical analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains those original model evaluations, ablations, and appendix experiments. Retention from v1 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical task synthesis, information-gap construction, mock-environment mapping, rubric-based rewards, and GRPO training procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic tool-use and ToolStar-derived reasoning training data, and the same 14 evaluation datasets/subsets spanning agentic tool use, mathematics, and search.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including the Qwen3 and ToolStar baselines in Tables 2–3, Qwen3-8B in Table 4, and the SFT comparison in Appendix B.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Appendix A, and Table 5 retain identical evaluation metrics, test sizes, model configurations, training settings, and testing procedures.

E4.justification: Table 4 ablations, simulator-size and demonstration-count analyses, Appendix B data-scaling and judge-stability experiments, and Appendix C examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report Avg@4 for TAU-2, Avg@6 for AIME24/AIME25/HMMT25, and the same six-repeat judge-score variance analysis on 100 tasks in Appendix B.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings match. For example, SYNTHAGENT-8B/14B averages remain 42.9/46.3 in Table 2 and 58.5/61.3 in Table 3; appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including the advantage-variance argument, information-gap formulation, finite mapping, and reward definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning synthetic tasks, stable mock environments, rubric-based training, and small-model performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including explanations of information gaps and simulator stability, and limitations arising from unavailable synthetic datasets and synthesis details from leading models.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data filtering, inference settings, and code/data access disclosures remain identical in the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and Appendix D retain the same cited works and positioning relative to prior agentic training, data synthesis, and environment simulation research.

P1.justification: The first author's displayed name changes from Yuan-Jay Lü to Yuanjie Lyu. The arXiv stamp updates from v1 dated 30 January 2026 to v2 dated 12 March 2026. Body prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and eight tables retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. The author-name and version-stamp edits do not change the page organization.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only author-name presentation and arXiv metadata. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and exposition—including all appendices—remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
